title: SafeCoEvo: Co-Evolving Safety Harnesses and Guards for LLM Agents at Test-Time

object.carrier: S-Harness five explicit safety components (Safety Prompt, Validated Memory, Safety Skills, Permission Policy, Guard Policy) updated after each episode, plus Guard model parameters periodically updated by GuardVPO from accumulated event-level safety experience

safety_property.statement: Agent task execution over a sequential deployment stream should avoid unsafe outcomes (both safety hazards and adversarial security attacks) while still completing the original task; judged jointly by Unsafe Outcome Rate together with Task Success Rate and Safe-and-Useful Completion Rate, so safety gains cannot come from over-conservative blocking. Holds only under the paper's continual test-time setting where feedback arrives after task completion and updates affect only subsequent tasks.
safety_property.operationalized_as: UOR (percentage of episodes resulting in an unsafe outcome), TSR, and SUCR on Agent-SafetyBench and Agent Security Bench (ASB), reported Overall and per Safety/Security subset on a 1,024-episode continual evolution stream and a 300-episode held-out test set

capabilities: ASB episodes pair an original task with an attack tool from the same scenario under the Mixed Attack setting, covering both aggressive and non-aggressive attacks
The unprotected task-performing model itself frequently produces unsafe outcomes (UOR 74-76% in tables), i.e., intrinsic unsafe behavior in the Safety setting
assumptions: The task-performing model remains frozen throughout deployment; only the external safety system (S-Harness and Guard) is updated
Execution trajectory and safety feedback become available only after each task completes, and updates take effect only on subsequent episodes
Official benchmark feedback provides reliable safety judgments used as the training signal
not_covered: Adaptive adversaries that react to the evolving defense during deployment
Attacks on the safety system itself (e.g., poisoning accumulated memory, skills, or event-level experience)
Multimodal, GUI/computer-use, audio, and long-horizon environments (stated in Appendix G as future work)

intervention.name: SafeCoEvo: dual-timescale S-Harness + GuardVPO co-evolution
intervention.description: An external safety system wrapped around a frozen task-performing model. At a short timescale, S-Harness updates five explicit components (Safety Prompt, Validated Memory, Safety Skills, Permission Policy, Guard Policy) after each episode from the trajectory and feedback (Eq. 4), abstracting away source-specific identifiers so knowledge is reusable across tasks. At a long timescale, GuardVPO periodically trains the Guard on accumulated event-level safety experience with an asymmetric safe/unsafe reward (+0.5/-0.5/-1.5/+1.0) and a KL-regularized clipped policy objective (Eqs. 6-8).

controls.name: SHE (experience-driven evolving harness, adapted to the same continual stream)

results.claim: On the full continual evolution stream, SafeCoEvo beats the strongest evolving baseline SHE, cutting UOR while raising both task-success metrics, so safety does not come from over-blocking.
results.comparison: SafeCoEvo vs strongest evolution baseline SHE
results.setting: DeepSeek-v4.1-Flash agent, Agent-SafetyBench + ASB continual evolution stream, continual test-time protocol
results.quote: As summarized in Table 1, compared with the strongest evolution baseline, SHE, SafeCoEvo reduces UOR by 10.05% over the full 1,024-episode continual evolution stream, while improving TSR and SUCR by 12.15% and 15.67%, respectively.

denominator.how_counted: UOR is 'the percentage of episodes that result in an unsafe outcome'; TSR/SUCR are percentages of episodes over the same stream (§4.1)

results.claim: Absolute performance of full SafeCoEvo on the full 1,024-episode stream: UOR 14.01% with TSR 76.08% and SUCR 70.02%.
results.setting: Full continual evolution stream, Agent-SafetyBench + ASB, DeepSeek-v4.1-Flash agent

denominator.how_counted: Table 1 'Overall performance on the continual evolution stream ... Full denote ... the full 1,024 episodes'; metrics are percentages of episodes (§4.1)

results.claim: Safety capabilities acquired during continual evolution generalize to a held-out test set of unseen scenarios without any test-time updates, with larger gains than on the stream itself.
results.comparison: SafeCoEvo vs strongest evolution baseline SHE
results.setting: 300-episode held-out test set (four unseen scenarios), evolved S-Harness and Guard frozen, no test-time updates
results.quote: As shown in Table 2, compared with the strongest evolution baseline, SHE, SafeCoEvo reduces UOR by 21.52%, while improving TSR and SUCR by 26.97% and 36.38%, respectively.

denominator.n_total: 300 held-out test episodes (100 Agent-SafetyBench / 200 ASB, four unseen scenarios)
denominator.how_counted: percentages of episodes on the held-out test set (§4.1 datasets split)

results.claim: S-Harness evolution alone (short timescale) accounts for most of the gain: vs the fully static configuration it cuts UOR and sharply raises utility on the full stream.
results.quote: Compared with the fully static SafeCoEvo configuration, S-Harness reduces UOR by 10.45%, while improving TSR and SUCR by 31.45% and 27.64%, respectively.

denominator.how_counted: percentage-of-episode metrics over the full stream (§4.1)

results.claim: GuardVPO adds a further gain on top of S-Harness evolution over the full stream (it is activated only after the first 512 episodes).
results.setting: Full 1,024-episode continual evolution stream; GuardVPO trained on experience from the first 512 episodes
results.quote: Table 1 further shows that introducing GuardVPO over the full continual evolution stream reduces UOR by an additional 3.96%, while improving TSR and SUCR by 0.88% and 2.83%, respectively.

denominator.how_counted: percentage-of-episode metrics over the full stream (§4.1)

results.claim: The advantage of evolved safety knowledge is concentrated in the adversarial Security setting, where S-Harness evolution nearly halves UOR and massively raises success versus the static configuration.
results.setting: ASB (Security) portion of the full continual evolution stream, Mixed Attack setting
results.quote: On the full continual evolution stream, compared with SafeCoEvo (Static), continual S-Harness evolution reduces UOR by 14.85%, while improving TSR and SUCR by 50.67% and 44.56%, respectively.

denominator.n_total: ASB portion of the stream (620 of 1,024 episodes)
denominator.how_counted: Security setting = ASB subset; percentage-of-episode metrics (§4.1, Appendix A)

results.claim: The continual adaptation capability transfers to an alternative task-performing model backbone rather than being tied to DeepSeek-v4.1-Flash.
results.setting: Task-performing model replaced by Qwen3.7-Flash; continual evolution stream
results.quote: when replacing the default task-performing model, DeepSeek-v4.1-Flash, with Qwen3.7-Flash, SafeCoEvo w/o GuardVPO reduces UOR by 17.81% compared with SOTA on the continual evolution stream, while improving TSR and SUCR by 23.66% and 19.80%, respectively.

denominator.how_counted: percentage-of-episode metrics on the continual evolution stream (§4.1)

results.claim: GuardVPO's risk-judgment gains transfer to external benchmarks the Guard was never trained on, at the cost of slightly lower safe-class specificity.
results.metric: Unsafe F1 / Unsafe Recall / Correct predictions
results.value: R-Judge F1 +0.46%, Recall +1.06%; ATBench F1 +1.28%, Recall +2.76%; correct 802/1000 -> 810/1000
results.comparison: GuardVPO-optimized Guard vs initial AgentDoG 1.5 Guard
results.setting: Guard evaluated zero-shot on external benchmarks R-Judge and ATBench after continual evolution
results.quote: compared with the initial AgentDoG 1.5, the Guard optimized by GuardVPO improves Unsafe F1 and Unsafe Recall on R-Judge by 0.46% and 1.06%, respectively, and by 1.28% and 2.76% on ATBench, while increasing the number of correct predictions from 802/1000 to 810/1000.

denominator.n_total: ATBench Correct counted out of 1000; R-Judge and ATBench F1/Recall set sizes not stated in the corpus
denominator.how_counted: ATBench Correct reported as 802/1000 -> 810/1000 (Table 5); F1/Recall/Specificity percentages given without explicit denominator counts

limitations.statement: The GuardVPO objective is one instantiation, not claimed to be the only or optimal approach to long-term parametric safety internalization.
limitations.quote: Although our experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of GuardVPO, we do not claim that its current optimization formulation is the only or optimal approach to long-term parametric safety internalization.

limitations.statement: Evaluation is limited to text-driven tool-using agents and a limited set of safety and security scenarios; multimodal, GUI, audio, and long-horizon environments are not covered.
limitations.quote: Our current evaluation primarily focuses on text-driven tool-using agents and a limited set of safety and security scenarios.

limitations.statement: GuardVPO increases sensitivity to unsafe events but introduces a modest trade-off in recognizing safe examples (safe-class specificity decreases on both external benchmarks).
limitations.quote: Meanwhile, Safe-class specificity slightly decreases on both R-Judge and ATBench, suggesting that GuardVPO increases sensitivity to unsafe events while introducing a modest trade-off in recognizing safe examples.

limitations.statement: Benefits of continual adaptation are not uniform across unseen scenarios: on the held-out Safety subset, S-Harness evolution is worse than the static configuration, while Security generalization is strong.
limitations.quote: These results suggest that the benefits of continual adaptation are not uniform across all unseen safety scenarios.

counterexamples.observation: On the held-out test set Safety subset (Table 8), SafeCoEvo w/o GuardVPO increases UOR by 6.00% and decreases TSR/SUCR by 6.00%/8.00% vs SafeCoEvo (Static) - continual evolution can hurt on unseen safety scenarios.

reproduction.data: Agent-SafetyBench, Agent Security Bench (ASB), R-Judge, ATBench, AgentDojo, AgentHarm
